title: Hierarchical deep compartment modeling: A workflow to leverage machine learning and Bayesian inference for hierarchical pharmacometric modeling

content.abstract_summary: Introduces Hierarchical Deep Compartment Modeling (HDCM), an extension of Deep Compartment Modeling (DCM) that integrates Bayesian inference (NUTS sampler via Turing.jl) to add IIV, residual error, and full uncertainty quantification — three features missing from vanilla DCM. DCM uses a neural network to map covariates to PK parameters but assesses no random effects, leading to overfitting and misspecification. HDCM addresses this by estimating IIV (log-normal, on CL, V2, ka) and proportional residual error jointly with NN weights via MCMC. Demonstrated on synthetic two-compartment oral data (30 subjects, 15 dense samples, 10 covariates). Open-source Julia workflow. Metrum Research Group.
key_findings: DCM (the predecessor architecture) does not evaluate any residual error or IIV — stated as primary failure mode leading to model misspecification and overfitting; HDCM adds both IIV and proportional residual error estimated jointly with NN weights via MCMC
Full Bayesian inference via NUTS (No U-Turn Sampler): 4 parallel chains × 1000 total samples (500 warmup + 500 sampling); all R-hat values ≤1.05; run time ~5 hours on synthetic dataset

Bayesian prior on NN weights (σ_w = 0.6) acts as regularizer, enabling stable training on small datasets (N=30) without significant overfitting: 'Bayesian analysis offered the added benefit of putting a penalty on the NN optimization via the prior information, which allows practitioners to train the NN on a small sample size without introducing significant overfitting'

Posterior estimates within reasonable range of true values: V2 error 5.06%, Q error 0.08%, ka error 25.4%, CL error 19.0%; IIV parameters recoverable (ω_CL median 0.13, ω_V2 median 0.09, ω_ka median 0.39) with wide credible intervals at N=30
SHAP implemented via ShapML.jl with Bayesian credible intervals: weight most influential for CL, but wide CIs at small N indicate SHAP interpretation requires larger datasets
BLQ handling included via left-censored likelihood (log-normal CDF); MAP initialization via Nelder-Mead as optional starting point
No real-world dataset validation performed — limitation explicitly stated; no benchmarking against NONMEM — both acknowledged as future work
limitations: Only tested on synthetic data; real-world application unvalidated — 'it is essential to test HDCM with real-world pharmacokinetic and pharmacodynamic datasets'
No benchmarking against NONMEM or other ML methods — 'Comparative studies are necessary'
Run time ~5 hours for 1000 MCMC samples on small synthetic dataset — potentially prohibitive for larger datasets or complex models
No sample size analysis; SHAP credible intervals are wide at N=30
IIV not added to all parameters (Q and V3 excluded in demonstration) — simplification not motivated

extracted_claims.text: DCM fell short in assessing residual errors and interindividual variability (IIV), potentially leading to model misspecification and overfitting. Furthermore, DCM lacked the ability to quantify model uncertainty.

Bayesian analysis offered the added benefit of putting a penalty on the NN optimization via the prior information, which allows practitioners to train the NN on a small sample size without introducing significant overfitting.
The high performance nature of the Julia language and the composability of the Julia workflow gives Julia an edge over other languages like Python and R.

numerical_findings.description: Typical PK parameter recovery error: V2, Q, CL, ka vs. true values
MCMC run time for N=30 synthetic dataset, 4 chains × 1000 samples
Residual error posterior: median and 95% CI

gaps_addressed: Directly fills M2.1 (Bayesian deep learning for PK): HDCM is the most complete implementation of Bayesian inference in a hybrid pharmacometric model available as open-source Julia workflow — adds full IIV + RUV + UQ to the DCM architecture

Extends and critiques janssen_2024 (deep compartment models): janssen_2024 added physiological constraints; HDCM adds Bayesian IIV/RUV — together they define the state-of-the-art in pharmacometric hybrid modeling

Provides a concrete criticism of DCM that the WG can use: 'DCM does not evaluate IIV or residual error' — motivating the HDCM work and framing why Bayesian approaches are necessary for regulatory-grade pharmacometric hybrid models

provenance.notes: Found via PubMed search 'Bayesian deep learning PK population UQ' (PMID 39402751). Full text retrieved from PMC11473376 (DOI: 10.1111/cts.70045). CTS 2024, 17(10):e70045. Open access. All 6 authors from Metrum Research Group (Tariffville, CT) — Kirouac D is senior author. Julia code available in Supplementary Materials. HDCM extends janssen_2024 by adding full Bayesian IIV/RUV; janssen_2024 extends lu_2021 by adding physiological constraints. This paper does NOT cite janssen_2024 explicitly (confirmed from extraction) but is architecturally an extension of the DCM line started by janssen_2024; relationship noted as extends.
